MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MAY 1, 2023

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR YOO at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Yoo, Olson, Romanelli, Nicklas, Friedman, Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Medawar

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, APRIL 3, 2023

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about the list of current uses that was going to be emailed
to the Planning Commission. Director Naughton stated that staff determined that it would be
more effective to provide a revised list of uses rather than the current list. The revised list of
permitted and conditionally permitted uses in the CG District will be emailed to the Planning
Commission soon.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES FOR THE MEETING OF APRIL
  3, 2023.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE - COMMERCIAL DISTRICT

Community Development Director Naughton provided a presentation with a summary of the staff
report. She stated that there were key procedural changes that were required to certify the
Housing Element, which include the elimination of Conditional Use Permits and Precise Plan of
Design for residential developments in the Commercial General (CG) and Commercial District
Mixed Use (CDMU) zones that meet the underlying zoning and general plan land use designation
criteria. Projects that utilize the City Community Benefit Density program will be required to enter

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 1, 2023
  1
 a discretionary, development agreement process. Also, any project that includes the subdivision
of land would also require a discretionary process.

Director Naughton stated that due to these changes, the objective is to build into the code all of
the things that would be reviewed through the discretionary review process, including objective
design standards.

Director Naughton posed the following questions for discussion:

Should a parking management plan be required for both rental and for-sale projects, in addition
to mixed-use projects?

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if this is for new rental or multi-unit for-sale residential projects.
Director Naughton stated that this is correct.

COMMISSIONER OLSON inquired about the extent of what would be required in a parking
management plan. Director Naughton stated that the developer could typically prepare a parking
management plan; some elements that would be included are the different uses, how many
parking spaces will be allocated within a shared garage or surface parking area. If it were a
condominium project, the parking management plan would be included in the CC&R’s.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that the City
has parking standards for the size of residential units, the number of parking spaces, and the
uses.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about how each project would be evaluated. Director
Naughton stated that staff would determine if the parking management plan reasonably provides
parking for the type of uses for the particular project.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that if a project were denied by staff, then the applicant
could appeal to the Planning Commission. Director Naughton agreed and added that there would
be specific components required in the parking management plan.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that a parking management plan should be required for
these projects.

Is it appropriate to include in the code a more restrictive measure for mixed-use projects?

Director Naughton stated that these include restricting the hours of noise inducing activities, such
as deliveries of commercial goods and supplies, and trash pick-up from 7am to 7pm for
Commercial District. The current code limits noise to commercial properties between 7am to
10pm.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER OLSON, Director Naughton stated that this is for
larger deliveries such as those using tractor trailers and would not include restricting small parcel
deliveries.

Should a threshold be established based on number of units, where a transportation impact
analysis is required?

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton stated that the
Level of Service (LOS) analysis was done by consultants and the city peer reviewed their work.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that from
staff’s perspective and direction received from the City Council during the General Plan Update
process, a transportation impact analysis should be required; the question is more-so in relation
to the size of project this should be required of.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if infrastructure changes would be reviewed by the Planning
Commission. Director Naughton stated that this would be only if the project needed to go through
a discretionary review process.

CHAIR YOO asked if there are any recent non-CEQA projects where the LOS was required.
Director Naughton stated that there have not been any recent projects; the larger projects were
approved and constructed prior to the VMT change, which went into effect in July of 2020.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about who had done the LOS transportation impact
analysis for the prior larger projects approved within the city. Director Naughton stated that each
project hired engineering firms and the city peer reviewed their work.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 1, 2023
  2
 CHAIR YOO inquired about what projects would require the LOS study. Director Naughton stated
that any project that required an initial study in CEQA.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked what other cities have used as their minimum number of
units. Director Naughton stated that she does not know, since the new VMT thresholds have gone
into effect, and stated that staff can do this research and bring this back to the Commission.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked if projects with 30du/acre or less could be exempt from having
to provide a traffic impact study. Director Naughton stated that the concern is that the LOS reviews
cumulative projects and stated that there should still be a review and analysis, and mitigation to
help the cumulative impact of projects.

COMMISSIONER FRIEDMAN commented that there are currently issues with flow of traffic and
these projects, even not more than 30du/acre would still have an impact and a transportation
impact analysis should be required since these projects would have required an initial study
previously.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked what type of project would have triggered an initial study under
CEQA. Director Naughton stated that it depends on the site and the physical impact of the project.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton explained that LOS
is based on trip generation rates and what this entails.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked the advantage of not having a threshold. Director
Naughton stated that smaller projects would not be required to provide this to make the process
easier for them.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that mixed-
use developments have non-residential units that are much smaller in relation to the number of
residential units. Projects with residential units are processed with the assumption of 30du/acre.
In addition, the commercial component would still be subject to a CUP and if the use is traffic
inducing, then staff would review VMT analysis and require a traffic impact analysis.

A discussion ensued on the Commission’s decision.

Director Naughton stated that she will inquire with the city’s Traffic Engineer on a recommended
threshold; there will need to be an objective standard and it may not need to be based on the
number of units. This item will be brought back to the Planning Commission for further discussion.

Does the code need to have specific requirement for a Maintenance Plan to address on-site litter
control for residential and mixed-use projects of all sized, or should this be folded into the CG
general standards?

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that at the last City Council meeting there were residents
present with complaints about litter in the Commercial District and does not seem that anyone is
being responsible for cleaning up.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that the CG
standards are part of the code and the Mixed-Use Overlay will have a separate set of standards.
This requirement could be applicable to all properties in the Commercial Zone and not just those
who are subject to a CUP.

Associate Planner Flores provided a presentation on the standards for Precise Plan of Design
review, which is the second discretionary permit that would no longer be required.

Associate Planner Flores posed the following questions for discussion:

What would be the appropriate maximum heights to establish?

Should we require architectural treatment on retaining walls over a certain height?

Should there be a list of prohibited fence and wall materials?

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that the
city currently does not have a height requirement for walls/fences in the Commercial District.

The only place where wall height is discussed is when a commercial project is adjacent to
residential and there is a five-foot solid wall required to be installed between the properties.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 1, 2023
  3
 In response to a question by COMMISSIONER YOO, Director Naughton stated that she has not
seen that neighboring cities are conducting comprehensive updates to their zoning codes. Staff
is currently reviewing other cities’ codes. The typical wall/fence height is six feet but could depend
on the site. Prohibiting materials may be more important.

Director Naughton stated that there are not height requirements for retaining walls. She provided
the example of the Brickwalk, if it were ever proposed for redevelopment, the hillside would need
to be addressed which would require very high retaining walls. It would be important to have
standards in the code should this project or a similar project be proposed.

CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that if there should be discretion on which walls would require certain
architectural treatments since some may be hidden from view from the street. Director Naughton
stated that the code could be written requiring retaining walls over a certain height that can be
viewed from the public right-of-way, would require architectural treatment and provide options.

CHAIR YOO commented that there generally is a preference for lower walls in the City and asked
about the maximum retaining wall height for residential districts. Director Naughton stated that it
is five feet. Currently, there are no maximum wall/retaining wall heights or grading provisions in
the commercial district and these need to be addressed in the zoning code update.

CHAIR YOO asked what would constitute going higher than five feet. Director Naughton stated
that site conditions may necessitate going higher.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that there should be architectural treatment for high walls, for
example walls over six feet.

Should there be a minimum percentage of landscaping along street frontages?

Should there be a common open space landscaping percentage required?

Associate Planner Flores stated that currently in the CG District there is a landscaping provision
for surface parking lot areas and staff is looking for direction on mixed-use development projects.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that
projects with a low setback requirement may still be able to meet a minimum landscape
requirement.

Director Naughton added that Community Services may be proposing a street tree plan for the
Commercial District, and it could be incorporated into the zoning code.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that staff should develop the plan and make it consistent with
setback requirements.

What would be the appropriate maximum height of light poles in surface parking lots? Should
there be flexible standards?

Should there be specific building-mounted lighting height requirements included in the code?

Is it appropriate to require a photometric plan for site and building-mounted lighting rather than
develop code standards?

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that
although this is not outlined in the zoning code; these are typically addressed in the conditions of
approvals for projects. There are exceptions for safety.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that with mixed-use projects, safety should be a
consideration. There may be some elements from the residential portion of the code to begin to
develop a policy for the Commercial District.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if there is an appropriate height for lighting in parking
areas. Director Naughton stated that she will discuss this with the Traffic Engineer before
returning with recommendations.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that lighting standards have changed with LED lights and
suggested not setting a specific standard since these could change year to year.

 In response to a question by COMMISSIONER FRIEDMAN, Director Naughton stated that
currently the photometric plan is not required for all projects; however, it was most recently

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 1, 2023
  4
 required for the pump station due to concern for the residents above the canyon.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked about the cost for a photometric plan. Director Naughton stated
that staff could find out and bring this back to the commission.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked if there are lighting requirements for residential areas on private
properties. Director Naughton stated that uplighting is prohibited and there are standards for
sports courts and the lighting standard is no higher than twelve feet.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that the Code Compliance Report is due at the next Planning
Commission meeting and asked if the report could include more detail. Director Naughton stated
that she conferred with the City Manager and City Attorney about this request and most code
enforcement cases do not have to do with conditions of approval or development standards and
are not within the purview of the Planning Commission or City Council unless it is to advise, in
closed session, if a case is moving forward to litigation. The bi-annual code enforcement report is
provided to keep the Planning Commission and City Council up to date on what is happening.
Some cases require discretionary entitlements or approvals that may come to the Planning
Commission to resolve a case and discussing these cases separately could further bias a
decision.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

NONE

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR YOO adjourned the meeting at 8:30 p.m.

The next Planning Commission meeting will be held on Monday, June 5, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.in the
City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Victor Yoo, Chair

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MAY 1, 2023
